items.title: catalog: custody

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

items.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/custody.yaml`, pinned to `Parker-Fawcett/custody@d4622ecfe791c6fc28ca5f800de5682df445a240`.

## What it does

Approvals judge a command by its text. The shell runs it by its semantics. Custody resolves the semantics first, then attributes the targets.

In #147373, `,` bound tighter than `+` in a PowerShell array literal. Five written paths became eight array elements, three of them profile roots. 188,303 delete records, 21.4 GiB, the user's Python install gone, no snapshot. Approval behaved exactly as implemented; the reviewer was never told what the command would touch.

Custody catches that before the prompt appears:

```
CUSTODY  7 targets, 4 outside this session

  X  C:\Windows\Temp                       the Windows directory
  X  ~/AppData/Local/Temp                  a local profile root
  X  ~/AppData/Local                       a local profile root
  .  ~/work/app/\pip\cache                 nothing at this path
  X  ~/AppData/Roaming                     a roaming profile root

  8,264 files, 2.2 MiB. No snapshot is taken before this runs.
  Why: ',' binds tighter than '+': 5 written path(s) became 8 array element(s)

  Approving deletes inside a local profile root, which this session did not create.
```

## Hermes surfaces used

- Hook `pre_tool_call`: resolves targets, returns `{"action": "approve", "message": <report>}` to add the report to Hermes's existing approval prompt. It never approves on its own. Unresolvable targets escalate rather than block, so a false positive costs one prompt.
- Hook `post_tool_call`: records the paths a write tool created, so the next call's attribution knows what the session owns.
- Hook `on_session_start`: takes a baseline of the working tree.
- Tools `custody_explain` (resolve a command without running it) and `custody_ledger` (what this session created, allowed, stopped).
- Bundled skill `custody:blast-radius`.
- `config_schema`: `mode` (`enforce` / `observe`) and `extra_protected`, editable from Settings → Plugins.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Reads outside the plugin's data directory.** Path metadata only (`os.scandir`, `os.stat`); file contents are never opened. Traversal is bounded per target at 120,000 entries and depth 8, skipping `node_modules`, `.git`, virtualenvs and build output. Needed to produce the file and byte counts in the report.
- **Local storage.** A SQLite ledger under `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/custody/`: this session's recorded writes, the baseline snapshot, and a decision log holding command text, verb, verdict and counts. Command text is stored because `custody_ledger` and `/custody` exist to answer "what did this session delete". Nothing is uploaded and nothing is pruned by the plugin.
- **Environment reads:** `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `USERPROFILE`, `WINDIR`, to expand paths. No credential stores, no `.env`, no `auth.json`.
- **No network, no shell execution, no background processes, no Python dependencies.**
- **Approvals.** Custody only adds a human step. There is no path where it approves, and no path where it runs the command it inspects.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate ./custody --install-deps` at the pinned commit: all checks pass, security scan `safe`, no core override. `hermes plugins doctor custody --ci`: 2 tools, 3 hooks.

Tests: 19 in the plugin repo (`python3 tests/test_custody.py`), including the #147373 command reproducing 5 written paths → 8 elements → 7 unique targets, and 16 benign commands producing no reports.

Repo: https://github.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody
